expectations.text: Uses gh issue list with label filter to discover issues
expectations.evidence: Step 1 shows: 'gh issue list -R <owner>/candles -l "ready-for-spec" --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments'

expectations.text: Analyzes dependencies between issues (explicit refs and implicit code overlap)
expectations.evidence: Step 2 covers explicit scanning and implicit analysis. Includes codebase exploration ('ls ~/Projects/candles/main/'), DAG construction, and cycle detection.

expectations.text: Presents issues in wave-based execution plan with parallel grouping
expectations.evidence: Step 2 shows wave grouping template. Step 4 shows a formatted plan with 3 waves.

expectations.text: Assigns pipeline modes (full/lite/quick) with reasoning tied to issue complexity
expectations.evidence: Step 3 shows criteria table. Plans include per-issue mode and reasoning.

expectations.text: Includes a user confirmation checkpoint before executing
expectations.evidence: Step 4 ends with 'I would wait for user confirmation before executing' with adjustment options.

expectations.text: Describes monitoring strategy using acorn status
expectations.evidence: Steps 5-6 show monitoring with acorn status, filesystem checks, progress reports, and failure handling.

expectations.text: Includes implementation handoff plan with worktree creation in wave order
expectations.evidence: Step 6 shows: acorn approve, dev wt, dev candles/<branch>/pi, sending specs to agents, dev pi-status monitoring.

expectations.text: Addresses merging between waves so agents see updated codebase
expectations.evidence: Explicitly covered: 'Wave N+1 specs must NOT start until Wave N implementations are merged into main' with git merge, Docker teardown, and dev cleanup commands. Key Design Decision #2 reinforces this.

claims.claim: Interleaved spec+implement cycle is necessary even for the spec phase
claims.evidence: Key insight section explains why you can't spec everything upfront: 'if issue #C depends on #A, and we spec #C before #A is implemented and merged, then #C's recon agents will examine the pre-#A codebase'

suggestions.reason: Baseline also passes all 8 assertions at 100%. The assertions don't capture qualitative differences. The baseline actually has a stronger theoretical insight about the interleaved spec+implement cycle. Consider assertions that test nuanced reasoning quality, not just structural elements.

eval_feedback.overall: Non-discriminating -- baseline matches the with-skill output on all structural assertions.
